title: The VR-AI–Assisted Simulation for Content Knowledge Application in Pre-Service EFL Teacher Training
extended_summary:
This paper investigates how pre-service English as a Foreign Language (EFL) teachers interpret and use a VR-AI–assisted simulation designed to support content knowledge application, with a specific focus on teaching the present perfect tense. The study is motivated by the challenge of preparing future teachers for real classroom demands, especially when they must explain grammar clearly, respond to spontaneous student questions, and adapt instruction under pressure.

The intervention combines high-immersion virtual reality with AI-generated learner questions in a simulated classroom. Participants taught a virtual class of intermediate students using the Virtual Speech platform and Oculus Quest 2, then completed a qualitative e-questionnaire about their experience. The study is framed by cognitive flexibility theory, emphasizing flexible knowledge application in unpredictable situations.

The participants were 17 female graduate students in a Master of Arts program in Teaching English as a Foreign Language at a university in Poland. They were preparing for school practicum in secondary education. The findings suggest that the simulation supported reflection, confidence building, and revision of grammar knowledge, while AI-generated questions were especially helpful in prompting deeper thinking and self-assessment. At the same time, participants reported limitations such as weak interaction, lack of teaching materials, technical issues, and anxiety. Overall, the paper concludes that VR combined with AI can be a valuable tool for teacher preparation, though greater interactivity and realism are still needed.

identified_tools.name: Virtual Speech
identified_tools.description: A commercial virtual reality application for role-play and professional development simulations, including AI-generated interactions in a simulated classroom.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the VR platform for a high-immersion simulated EFL classroom in which pre-service teachers taught the present perfect tense and answered AI-generated questions from virtual students.

findings.finding_summary: In this qualitative case study with pre-service EFL teachers (N=17), participants generally reported that the simulation supported reflection, confidence, and the application of grammar knowledge, but some also reported technological difficulties, lack of interaction, and limits to transferability to real classrooms. The paper does not report quantitative effect sizes.
findings.measure: Participant reflections on teaching performance, content knowledge application, and transferability to real-world teaching

findings.finding_summary: Participants reported operational challenges including lack of student feedback, absence of teaching materials, VR equipment issues, and difficulties using the virtual board. The paper qualitatively notes these as barriers to the teaching experience rather than quantifying their prevalence or magnitude.
findings.measure: Participant-reported technological and instructional constraints during the VR simulation

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative case study with a small sample and no quantitative causal estimate. It provides useful descriptive evidence about teacher perceptions and feasibility, but not experimental evidence of effectiveness.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports perceived benefits such as improved confidence and reflection, but these are subjective and not quantified. Reported risks and limitations are also substantial, so overall impact is unclear rather than demonstrably large.
